newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE gas oil overbought but may test $200.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE gas oil overbought but may test $200.

text.p: After charging to 4-1/2 month highs on Thursday, IPE gas oil futures may extend those gains and test the highs for the year just above $200 a tonne, even though some chartists warned the market was clearly overbought.
Oct Brent is also set to test its contract high of $20.98 a barrel after two days of sharp gains that lifted prices through a minor double top on Thursday at $20.80. It settled at $20.75.
"The rapid recovery from this week's brief consolidation has once again put this market into overbought territory," said Nick Wilson, technical analyst at MeesPierson.

"Our initial objective of $196 (basis Oct) is likely to be achieved today after which we would expect a longer period of consolidation," he said, adding his objectives for Sept were met yesterday. "Our medium to longer term view remains bullish."
Oct gas oil ended Thursday at $194.25 and was up 50 cents at $194.75 at the open today. Sept gained $1.25 to $198.
"The readings are getting a bit high," he said. "It is vulnerable to some sort of consolidation but I don't think it will pull back too far."

Coming into today, Sept gas oil's nine- and 14-day Relative Strength Index levels were at 82 and 77 percent, the highest levels for the spot contract this year. But there was no divergence during Thursday's rally as higher price levels were accompanied by higher momentum levels.

Resistance for Sept gas oil is at its contract high of $198.50, the psychological $200 level that was also a previous high on the spot chart from April, and then at the year's high of $200.50 from March, analysts said.
"Generally the market still looks constructive but it is dangerous ahead of a long weekend because we've got a herd instinct and herds can turn on a dime," said one oil broker.
He said $200-$201 was a possibility but much will depend on New York's direction as well as "the perception of how the market wants to be positioned going into the long weekend."
On the downside, Sept gas oil should find support at $195.75, $194.25 and $193.75, another broker said.
Wilson expected Oct Brent, after closing Thursday at $20.75, to score new contract highs, which in turn would begin to fill a gap on the spot chart that runs to an April 15 low of $21.27.

"The reluctance of the market to test even minor support this week at $19.87 reinforces our bullish view and we continue to expect new contract highs within the next few trading days," he said. "Our next upside objective is $21.55."
